summary: Xu Dishan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Yenching University, Columbia University, and the University of Oxford. He held posts at Peking University, Tsinghua University, and the University of Hong Kong.

Xue Yu is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MPhil from the University of Hong Kong. His posts include assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and visiting positions at the University of Chicago and PBIS.

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu, and is attested as an associate professor at Renmin University of China in 2015.

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Shoryu Katsura, was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011, and served as a research associate at the China Tibetology Research Center.
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies, serving and studying as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington under Gregory Schopen, David Dean Shulman, and others. She holds a professorship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS University of London under David Friedman. He served as Director and Emeritus Professor at PGIPBS and held visiting professorships internationally.
Yandong Hou is a Tibetology scholar who studied at and held a post at the Nanjing Institute of Geography and Limnology.

Yanfei Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Zhao earned master's degrees from Beijing Foreign Studies University and SOAS University of London, and pursued doctoral studies at BFSU and as a visiting PhD student at Yale University.
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. Zhou completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and also studied under Hojin.
Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetology scholar who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London between ~2000 and 2004 under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Yannick Laurent works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Laurent has held posts at the University of Munich and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu from ~1935 to 1941 and under Yinshun from ~1941 to 1947.
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar of Tibetology and sinology. He studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of California in 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou works in Buddhist and religious studies, completing a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, was a Mellon postdoctoral fellow at Washington University in St. Louis, and became a professor at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.
